title: Saudi Arabia's Big-Spending Era Winds Down Amid Vision 2030 Scrutiny
detail: NYT analysis examines Saudi Arabia's retreat from mega-investments in sports (LIV Golf) and global prestige projects, raising questions about the future of Vision 2030 and the kingdom's regional influence as the big-spending era appears to be winding down. The report notes scaling back of NEOM's 'The Line,' reduced commitments to international sports deals, and growing pressure on the Public Investment Fund to prioritize financial returns over geopolitical prestige.

title: Saudi Arabia Positioned for Oil Revenue Windfall as Hormuz Disruptions Lift Prices
detail: Bloomberg analysis finds Saudi Arabia well-positioned to benefit financially from Strait of Hormuz disruptions caused by the ongoing US-Iran conflict. With Saudi Arabia exporting the bulk of its crude through the Red Sea route via the East-West Pipeline, higher global oil prices more than compensate for any logistical disruption, giving Riyadh a competitive revenue advantage over Gulf neighbors more dependent on the Persian Gulf export route. Saudi Arabia is the only major Gulf producer with meaningful Red Sea crude export capacity.

media.caption: Bloomberg: Saudi Arabia gains competitive oil revenue advantage as Hormuz disruptions drive prices higher
